title: Is that then the divine substance wherein Father and Son are consubstantial? Where is poor dear Arius to try conclusions?
html_source: Stephen has been slowly becoming more and more of a rebel against society and the Church as time has progressed. He first started thinking about various Christian heretics like Arius, the “Jesus Ain’t God” guy, in Chapter One (not the exact line, but the paragraph containing it).

anchor.text: Is that then the divine substance wherein Father and Son are consubstantial? Where is poor dear Arius to try conclusions?
anchor.prefix: with ashes on her breath. They clasped and sundered, did the coupler's will. From before the ages He willed me and now may not will me away or ever. A lex eterna stays about Him.
